theorem_title: Fischler 2001, Theorem 4.1 in pencil form (orbit dimensions read as ranks of M_α, M_x; suitability as in the pencil form of Prop. 3.1); not printed in this form
formal_statement:
open Complex ComplexConjugate

namespace DiazModulus

theorem fischler_theorem_4_1_pencil {d l k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (F : Fin l → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
    (hF : ∀ a i j, F a i j ∈ Qbar) (hinj : LinearIndependent (↥Qbar) F)
    (hfix : ∀ φ : Fin d → ℂ, (∀ i, φ i ∈ Qbar) → (∀ a, Matrix.vecMul φ (F a) = 0) → φ = 0)
    (α : Fin d → ℂ) (hα : d < (Matrix.of fun i a => ((F a).mulVec α) i).rank + k)
    (x : Fin d → ℂ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ LogAlgTilde)
    (hr : (d + l) * (Matrix.of fun i a => ((F a).mulVec x) i).rank < d * l)
    (hrk : k * (Matrix.of fun i a => ((F a).mulVec x) i).rank ≤ d) :
    ∃ φ : Fin d → ℂ, (∀ i, φ i ∈ Qbar) ∧ φ ≠ 0 ∧ φ ⬝ᵥ x = 0 := by
  sorry

end DiazModulus
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 4.1 (pp. 174–175), in pencil form; not printed in this form, with the dictionary of the pencil form of Prop. 3.2 (DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_2_pencil). The printed hypotheses (k > 1; (ρ, X) suitable; a ρ-orbit of codimension less than k in W; X of dimension r ≤ d/k) become k ≥ 2, (S1′)–(S3′) as in the pencil form of Prop. 3.1, d − rk M_α < k for some α, and k·rk M_x ≤ d, orbit dimensions being read as ranks (Lemma 2.4). Hyperplanes are vector hyperplanes (convention of p. 169). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The proof is the printed one (p. 175), its arithmetic cleared of denominators. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_prop_3_1_pencil. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 20 November 2026 (C. Perassi).
